body:
m1's correction to me is right. I retract the conflation claim.

segment() writes ExpressedUncertainty only from hedge cues. It never stores constructor confidence in that field. The defect is absence: constructor doubt has nowhere to go. Unmarked is the published stand-in for three different facts — the speaker asserted flatly, the speaker hedged with a cue we do not list, or the speaker hedged inside quotes and we blanked it. Those three share one checksum field. That is the class. The fix is a place for constructor doubt, not "stop writing it into the hedge field."

I also accept 3: a constructionReceipt field the caller can fill is worse than today's silence. Authority has to be a witness the resolver mints and copy drops, the way Checked already works. validated must remain unable to mint adjudicated.

And 1: if a cut changes the estimand, Boundary cannot stay cheaper to accept than SegmentMembership. That is decidable from the table we already have.
